questions.question: What is the object of the yoga system Kapila explains at the beginning of this chapter?
questions.explanation: "Now I shall explain to you the system of yoga, the object of which is to concentrate the mind." (SB 3.28.1)

questions.question: One should be satisfied with as much gain as one achieves by the grace of the Lord, and one should worship what?

options.text: The lotus feet of a spiritual master

questions.explanation: "One should be satisfied with as much gain as he achieves by the grace of the Lord, and one should worship the lotus feet of a spiritual master." (SB 3.28.2)

questions.question: After withdrawing the senses from sense objects, where should the yogi concentrate the mind?
questions.explanation: "One must observe silence, acquire steadiness by practicing different yogic postures, control the breathing of the vital air, withdraw the senses from sense objects and thus concentrate the mind on the heart." (SB 3.28.5)

questions.question: Fixing the vital air and the mind in one of how many circles of vital air circulation is called samadhi?
questions.explanation: "Fixing the vital air and the mind in one of the six circles of vital air circulation within the body... is called samadhi." (SB 3.28.6)

questions.question: By practicing pranayama, one can eradicate the contamination of what?
questions.explanation: "By practicing the process of pranayama, one can eradicate the contamination of his physiological condition." (SB 3.28.11)

questions.question: By meditating on the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one can become free from what?

options.text: The three modes of material attachment

questions.explanation: "By meditating on the Supreme Personality of Godhead one can become free from the three modes of material attachment." (SB 3.28.11)

questions.question: How is the body of the Supreme Personality of Godhead described in the meditation Kapila teaches?

options.text: Swarthy like the petals of a blue lotus

questions.explanation: "He has... a swarthy body like the petals of a blue lotus." (SB 3.28.13)

questions.question: On His breast the Lord bears which mark?

options.text: The mark of Srivatsa, a curl of white hair

questions.explanation: "On His breast He bears the mark of Srivatsa, a curl of white hair." (SB 3.28.14)

questions.question: What gem is suspended from the Lord's neck?
questions.explanation: "The brilliant Kaustubha gem is suspended from His neck." (SB 3.28.14)

questions.question: The yogi should not take a collective view of all the Lord's limbs, but should do what?

options.text: Fix the mind on each individual limb of the Lord
Concentrate on the Lord's face only
View only the form as a whole

questions.explanation: "The yogi should not take a collective view of all His limbs, but should fix the mind on each individual limb of the Lord." (SB 3.28.20)

questions.question: On which part of the Lord should the devotee first concentrate his mind, adorned with marks of a thunderbolt, goad, banner and lotus?
questions.explanation: "The devotee should first concentrate his mind on the Lord's lotus feet, which are adorned with the marks of a thunderbolt, a goad, a banner and a lotus." (SB 3.28.21)

questions.question: The holy waters of the Ganges, borne on Lord Siva's head, have their source in what?

options.text: The water that washed the Lord's lotus feet

questions.explanation: "Lord Siva becomes all the more blessed by bearing on his head the holy waters of the Ganges, which has its source in the water that washed the Lord's lotus feet." (SB 3.28.22)

questions.question: The Lord's thighs are described as the storehouse of what?
questions.explanation: "The yogi should fix his mind in meditation on the Personality of Godhead's thighs, the storehouse of all energy." (SB 3.28.24)

questions.question: From the Lord's navel, which is the foundation of the entire universe, sprang what?

options.text: The lotus stem containing all the different planetary systems

questions.explanation: "From His navel, which is the foundation of the entire universe, sprang the lotus stem containing all the different planetary systems." (SB 3.28.25)

questions.question: The Lord's chest is described as the source of what?

options.text: All transcendental pleasure for the mind and full satisfaction for the eyes

questions.explanation: "The Lord's chest is the source of all transcendental pleasure for the mind and full satisfaction for the eyes." (SB 3.28.26)

questions.question: The Lord's four arms are the source of what?

options.text: All the powers of the demigods who control material nature

questions.explanation: "The yogi should further meditate upon the Lord's four arms, which are the source of all the powers of the demigods who control the various functions of material nature." (SB 3.28.27)

questions.question: The pearl necklace on the Lord's neck is considered to represent whom?

options.text: The pure living entities who are always engaged in His service

questions.explanation: "The pearl necklace on the Lord's neck, which is considered to represent the pure living entities who are always engaged in His service." (SB 3.28.28)

questions.question: When the mind is completely freed from material contamination and detached, what is it compared to?
questions.explanation: "When the mind is thus completely freed from all material contamination and detached from material objectives, it is just like the flame of a lamp." (SB 3.28.35)

questions.question: The perfectly realized soul discovers that pleasure and pain are actually due to what?

options.text: The false ego, which is a product of ignorance

questions.explanation: "He discovers that pleasure and pain as well as their interactions, which he attributed to his own self, are actually due to the false ego, which is a product of ignorance." (SB 3.28.36)

questions.question: A yogi should see the same soul in all manifestations because all that exists is what?

options.text: A manifestation of different energies of the Supreme

questions.explanation: "A yogi should see the same soul in all manifestations, for all that exists is a manifestation of different energies of the Supreme." (SB 3.28.42)
